**Summary of Medical Sources Gathered for Week 2 (Days 8-14 Postpartum)**

### What I Did
- Conducted targeted web searches for each specified topic: breastfeeding establishment, maternal physical recovery (lochia and perineal healing), newborn jaundice, and maternal emotional adjustment, focusing on the days 8-14 postpartum period.
- Attempted to extract full content from key sources using the `web_extract` tool, but the tool failed due to the search-only backend limitation (Brave Search free tier cannot extract URL content; would require configuring an extraction backend like firecrawl, tavily, etc.).
- Compiled a list of authoritative sources from search result snippets, prioritizing clinical guidelines, peer-reviewed articles, and reputable health organization pages.

### What I Found / Accomplished
**Breastfeeding Establishment (Days 8-14)**
- StatPearls (Postpartum Care of the New Mother) recommends postpartum visits at 7-14 days to assess breastfeeding progress.
- La Leche League emphasizes 8+ feedings/24 hours in the first month to establish milk supply.
- KDHE Kansas document "Breastfeeding at 2 Weeks" provides specific counseling guidance for this timeframe.
- CDC notes that milk supply typically regulates around 4 weeks, but establishment patterns are critical in weeks 1-2.

**Maternal Physical Recovery**
- **Lochia**: Cleveland Clinic and StatPearls indicate lochia transitions to creamy/yellowish-white (lochia alba) around days 10-14; normal duration up to 3-4 weeks.
- **Perineal Healing**: Family Doctor states perineal stitches typically absorb in 7-10 days; UnityPoint notes discharge becomes yellowish-white mucous by ~2 weeks; StatPearls advises waiting 4-6 weeks before resuming sexual activity for complete healing.

**Newborn Jaundice (Days 8-14)**
- American Pregnancy Association and AAFP note breast milk jaundice may peak or show a secondary rise around day 14.
- PMC article defines prolonged neonatal jaundice as lasting >14-21 days (seen in up to 15% of newborns).
- NCBI Bookshelf highlights that prolonged jaundice beyond 14 days is more common in breastfed babies.
- Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic observe that jaundice in breastfed infants can last a month or longer.

**Maternal Emotional Adjustment (Days 8-14)**
- Newton-Wellesley Hospital and StatPearls describe normal feelings of being overwhelmed; recommend postpartum visit at 7-14 days for emotional/mental health screening.
- Secure Beginnings and March of Dimes note Baby Blues typically peaks days 3-5 and resolves by ~2 weeks.
- Progyny explains hormonal shifts (oxytocin/endorphin rise, estrogen/progesterone drop) influencing emotional adjustment.

### Files Created or Modified
No files were created or modified. The available tools (`web_search`, `web_extract`) do not include file creation/write capabilities. All gathered information is summarized above.

### Issues Encountered
- The `web_extract` tool failed when attempting to retrieve full page content due to the backend being limited to search-only (Brave Search free tier). This prevented direct extraction of detailed text from the identified sources.
- Despite this limitation, the search results provided sufficient snippet information to identify highly relevant, authoritative sources for each subtopic.
- No access to subscription-based journals or paywalled articles was possible; all sources are freely available or from government/educational domains (.gov, .nih, .org).
